intro: Welcome back! You can already imagine the present with the second conditional: If I had more time, I would learn Japanese. Today you go back in time and imagine a different past: If I had known about the meeting, I would have come (but I didn't know, and I didn't come). Then you'll connect a different past to a different now: If I had studied IT, I would have a different job now.
teachingNotes: Recap in one line, don't re-teach: from b1-first-conditional and b1-second-conditional the learner knows if + present, will (real possibility) and if + past simple, would + base verb (imagined now: If I had more time, I would learn Japanese = I don't have more time). From b1-past-perfect they know had + third form (past participle) and that 'd before a third form = had. New: third conditional = if + past perfect, would have + third form, for an imagined PAST that did not happen: If I had known, I would have come = I didn't know, and I didn't come. Both parts are untrue. Indonesian marks this with words (seandainya dulu, kalau saja waktu itu) and keeps the verb; English moves the verb 'two steps back': had known, would have come. Negative hadn't / wouldn't have; question What would you have done if ...?; the if-part can come first (comma) or second (no comma).

Common errors and why: *'If I knew about the meeting, I would have come' -> 'If I had known ...' (past simple in the if-part = imagined NOW, the second conditional; the past needs the past perfect). *'If I would have studied harder, I would have passed' -> 'If I had studied harder ...' (no would in the if-part, as in the first and second conditional; mention that this is heard in casual American speech, but it's not standard and is marked wrong in writing and tests). *'would have went / would have saw' -> would have gone / seen (third form after have). *'would of' is a spelling mistake for would've.

could have / might have replace would have in the result: could have + third form = 'bisa' (it was possible, there was a chance), might have = 'mungkin' (perhaps, not sure). Contractions in speech: 'd = had OR would. Teach the test: in the if-part 'd is always had (never would after if); 'd + have + third form = would (I'd have come); 'd + third form (known, gone, been) = had (I'd known). would have sounds like would've ('wud-ev'), often very weak. Don't teach 'd had (had had) unless asked.

Mixed conditional (objective use-mixed-conditionals): an imagined past with a result NOW: if + past perfect, would + base verb (or would be + -ing for something in progress now): If I had studied IT, I would have a different job now. Common error: *'I would be live in Jakarta now' -> 'I would be living / I would live in Jakarta now' (would be + -ing, or would + base verb; never would be + base verb). Also *'would have been tired now' -> 'would be tired now'. Time words decide: yesterday, last year, in 2019 -> would have + third form; now, today, at the moment, still -> would + base verb. Only test cases where a time word makes one type clearly right. As a NOTE only (not tested): a present condition with a past result: If I spoke Japanese, I would have applied for the Tokyo job last year (I don't speak Japanese, in general).

At B2 many choices depend on meaning: If I had taken the job, I would have moved to Jakarta (then) and ... I would be living in Jakarta (now) are both correct with different meanings. Accept both when no time word decides, and explain the difference. Limits: no wish / if only, no should have / must have (past modals of advice and deduction come in other lessons), no inversion (Had I known ...), no but for / otherwise. If the learner asks, say these come later. B2 contexts: work, study abroad, job offers, missed flights, KRL/MRT, ojek online, Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya, rupiah.

keyPoints.title: An imagined past: if + had + third form, would have + third form
keyPoints.explanation: To imagine a past that did not happen, use if + past perfect (had + third form), would have + third form. If I had known, I would have come = I didn't know, so I didn't come. Both parts are untrue. Don't use the past simple in the if-part ('If I knew' is about now) and never put would after if ('If I would have studied' is wrong). could have = it was possible; might have = maybe. In speech 'd = had in the if-part (If I'd known) and would before have (I'd have come).

examples.en: If I had known about the meeting, I would have come.
examples.id: Seandainya waktu itu saya tahu soal rapatnya, saya pasti datang.

examples.en: If we hadn't missed the bus, we wouldn't have been late.
examples.id: Kalau saja kami tidak ketinggalan bus, kami tidak akan terlambat.

examples.en: If she'd asked me, I could have helped her.
examples.id: Seandainya dulu dia minta tolong, saya bisa membantunya.

id.title: Masa lalu khayalan: if + had + bentuk ketiga, would have + bentuk ketiga
id.explanation: Untuk membayangkan masa lalu yang tidak terjadi, pakai if + past perfect (had + bentuk ketiga), would have + bentuk ketiga. If I had known, I would have come = saya tidak tahu, jadi saya tidak datang. Kedua bagiannya tidak nyata. Jangan pakai past simple di bagian if ('If I knew' itu tentang sekarang) dan jangan pernah pakai would setelah if ('If I would have studied' salah). could have = waktu itu bisa; might have = mungkin. Saat bicara, 'd = had di bagian if (If I'd known) dan = would sebelum have (I'd have come).

keyPoints.title: Mixed: a different past, a different now
keyPoints.explanation: When an imagined past changes the present, use if + past perfect, would + base verb (or would be + -ing): If I had studied IT, I would have a different job now. Time words decide: now, today, still → would + base verb; yesterday, last year → would have + third form. Not 'would be live' but would be living or would live. Less common, the other way round: If I spoke Japanese (in general), I would have applied for the job last year.

examples.en: If I had studied IT, I would have a different job now.
examples.id: Seandainya dulu saya kuliah IT, sekarang pekerjaan saya pasti lain.

examples.en: If I had taken that job, I would be living in Jakarta now.
examples.id: Seandainya dulu saya ambil pekerjaan itu, sekarang saya tinggal di Jakarta.

examples.en: If Budi hadn't lost his passport, he would be in Tokyo today.
examples.id: Kalau saja Budi tidak kehilangan paspornya, hari ini dia sudah ada di Tokyo.

id.title: Mixed: masa lalu berbeda, masa kini berbeda
id.explanation: Kalau masa lalu yang dibayangkan mengubah masa kini, pakai if + past perfect, would + kata kerja dasar (atau would be + -ing): If I had studied IT, I would have a different job now. Kata waktu yang menentukan: now, today, still → would + kata kerja dasar; yesterday, last year → would have + bentuk ketiga. Bukan 'would be live', tapi would be living atau would live. Lebih jarang, kebalikannya: If I spoke Japanese (secara umum), I would have applied for the job last year.

guidedPractice.hint: She didn't check (the past, not real): had + third form. The imagined past result: would have + third form (take → took → taken).

assessment.prompt: Last month Rina missed her flight to Bali because the KRL broke down. Complete with the verbs in brackets (use the negative): If the KRL ___ (not / break) down, she ___ (not / miss) her flight.
acceptableAnswers: hadn't broken wouldn't have missed
had not broken would not have missed
hadn't broken would not have missed
had not broken wouldn't have missed
hadn't broken wouldn't've missed
assessment.rubric: Correct: hadn't broken (past perfect: an imagined past) + wouldn't have missed (would have + third form). 'didn't break ... wouldn't have missed' = 40 (past simple in the if-part is about now). 'hadn't broke' = 70 (third form of break is broken). 'wouldn't miss' = 40 (that's about now, but the flight was last month). 'wouldn't have miss' = 70.

'If I left home earlier, I would have caught ...' = 40 (past simple = the second conditional). 'If I had left ..., I would catch the train' = 50. 'would have catched' = 70 (catch → caught → caught). 'If I had had Budi's number' is also correct. 'I would have called him' = 70 (correct third conditional, but bisa = could). 'If I knew Budi's number, I could call him' = 30 (that's about now). 'If I knew ..., I could have called' = 50. 'could have call' = 70.

assessment.prompt: Budi failed his driving test last week, so right now he's standing on a crowded bus. Complete with would and the verb in brackets: If he had passed the test, he ___ (drive) to work right now.
acceptableAnswers: would be driving
'd be driving
would drive
'd drive
assessment.rubric: Correct: would be driving (or would drive): an imagined past (had passed) with a result right now → would + base verb, or would be + -ing for something happening now. 'would have driven' = 30 (that's a past result, but the sentence says right now). 'would be drive' = 40 (would be + -ing, not the base verb). 'will drive' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: If I hadn't stayed up so late last night, I wouldn't have been tired now.
acceptableAnswers: if i hadn't stayed up so late last night i wouldn't be tired now

if i hadn't stayed up so late last night i would not be tired now

i wouldn't be tired now if i hadn't stayed up so late last night

assessment.rubric: Correct: ... I wouldn't be tired now (the past part stays: hadn't stayed up last night; the result is about now → would + base verb). 'I won't be tired now' = 20. Removing 'now' and keeping 'wouldn't have been tired' = 50 (a correct third conditional, but the item is about the present result). Changing the if-part to 'didn't stay up' = 30.

assessment.prompt: Sari didn't sleep at all last night, and now she can't concentrate at work. Complete what she says with the verb in brackets: 'If I ___ (sleep) better last night, I wouldn't feel so tired today.'
acceptableAnswers: had slept
'd slept
if i had slept better last night i wouldn't feel so tired today
if i'd slept better last night i wouldn't feel so tired today
assessment.rubric: Correct: had slept / 'd slept (last night is the past, and it's imagined → past perfect; sleep → slept → slept). 'slept' = 30 (past simple in the if-part = imagined now, but last night is past). 'would have slept' = 0 (no would in the if-part). 'had sleep' = 60.

material.title: Recap, then one step further back

blocks.text:
**Quick recap:** you know two conditionals. The **first** is for real possibilities (*If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home*). The **second** imagines the **present**: *If I had more time, I would learn Japanese* (= I don't have more time).

Now something new: imagining the **past**. Something happened (or didn't), and you imagine a different version. English uses the **third conditional**:
- **if + past perfect** (*had + third form*: had known, had left, hadn't missed)
- **would have + third form** (*would have come, would have passed*)

*If I had known about the meeting, I would have come.*

The **third form** (past participle) is the form you use after *have / had*: *know → knew → **known**, go → went → **gone***. Negative: **hadn't** / **wouldn't have**. Question: **What would you have done if …?**

id.text:
**Ulasan singkat:** kamu sudah kenal dua conditional. **First** untuk kemungkinan nyata (*If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home*). **Second** berandai-andai tentang **sekarang**: *If I had more time, I would learn Japanese* (= saya tidak punya lebih banyak waktu).

Sekarang hal baru: berandai-andai tentang **masa lalu**. Sesuatu sudah terjadi (atau tidak terjadi), dan kamu membayangkan versi lainnya. Bahasa Inggris memakai **third conditional**:
- **if + past perfect** (*had + bentuk ketiga*: had known, had left, hadn't missed)
- **would have + bentuk ketiga** (*would have come, would have passed*)

*If I had known about the meeting, I would have come.*

**Bentuk ketiga** (past participle) adalah bentuk yang dipakai setelah *have / had*: *know → knew → **known**, go → went → **gone***. Negatif: **hadn't** / **wouldn't have**. Pertanyaan: **What would you have done if …?**

rows.en: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.
rows.id: Kalau besok hujan, saya di rumah saja.
rows.note: first: if + present, will → real, can happen

id.note: first: if + present, will → nyata, bisa terjadi

rows.en: If I had more time, I would learn Japanese.
rows.id: Seandainya saya punya lebih banyak waktu, saya akan belajar bahasa Jepang.
rows.note: second: if + past, would + verb → imagined now

id.note: second: if + past, would + verb → khayalan, sekarang

rows.en: If I had known about the meeting, I would have come.
rows.id: Seandainya waktu itu saya tahu soal rapatnya, saya pasti datang.
rows.note: third (new): if + had + third form, would have + third form → imagined past

id.note: third (baru): if + had + bentuk ketiga, would have + bentuk ketiga → khayalan, masa lalu

blocks.text:
**Why had + third form when it's just 'the past'?** In the second conditional, the verb takes **one step back** from reality: present → past (*If I had more time* = now). For the past, there's no room left in the past simple, so the verb takes **one more step back**: past → **past perfect** (*If I had known* = then). That's why *If I knew* is about **now**, and *If I had known* is about **then**.
**Both parts didn't happen:** *If I had known, I would have come* = I **didn't** know, and I **didn't** come.
Indonesian shows the past with words (*seandainya dulu, kalau saja waktu itu*) and keeps the verb. English shows it in the **verb**.

id.text:
**Kenapa had + bentuk ketiga, padahal cuma 'masa lalu'?** Di second conditional, kata kerjanya **mundur satu langkah** dari kenyataan: present → past (*If I had more time* = sekarang). Untuk masa lalu, past simple sudah 'terpakai', jadi kata kerjanya **mundur satu langkah lagi**: past → **past perfect** (*If I had known* = dulu). Karena itu *If I knew* tentang **sekarang**, dan *If I had known* tentang **waktu itu**.
**Kedua bagiannya tidak terjadi:** *If I had known, I would have come* = saya **tidak** tahu, dan saya **tidak** datang.
Bahasa Indonesia menunjukkan masa lalu dengan kata (*seandainya dulu, kalau saja waktu itu*) dan kata kerjanya tetap. Bahasa Inggris menunjukkannya lewat **kata kerja**.

rows.en: If we hadn't missed the bus, we wouldn't have been late.

id.title: Ulasan singkat, lalu mundur satu langkah lagi

material.title: Two traps, and could have / might have

blocks.text:
**Trap 1: the past simple in the if-part.** *If I knew about the meeting, I would have come* ✗. *If I knew* is the second conditional: it's about **now**. For the past, use **had + third form**: *If I **had known** about the meeting, I would have come* ✓.

**Trap 2: would in the if-part.** *If I would have studied harder, I would have passed* ✗ → *If I **had studied** harder, I would have passed* ✓. As in every conditional you know, **would** goes only in the result part.

**After would have, use the third form:** *would have **gone*** (not *would have went*), *would have **seen*** (not *would have saw*).

id.text:
**Jebakan 1: past simple di bagian if.** *If I knew about the meeting, I would have come* ✗. *If I knew* itu second conditional: tentang **sekarang**. Untuk masa lalu, pakai **had + bentuk ketiga**: *If I **had known** about the meeting, I would have come* ✓.

**Jebakan 2: would di bagian if.** *If I would have studied harder, I would have passed* ✗ → *If I **had studied** harder, I would have passed* ✓. Sama seperti semua conditional yang sudah kamu kenal, **would** hanya ada di bagian hasil.

**Setelah would have, pakai bentuk ketiga:** *would have **gone*** (bukan *would have went*), *would have **seen*** (bukan *would have saw*).

blocks.text:
Why do Indonesian speakers make these mistakes? *Seandainya dulu saya tahu* has no tense, and *akan* covers will and would, so learners put *would* in both parts or use the simple past. Check the **if-part**: past situation → **had + third form**, and no *would*.
You may hear *If I would have known* in casual American speech, but it isn't standard: in writing, at work and in tests, use **If I had known**.

id.text:
Kenapa penutur bahasa Indonesia sering membuat kesalahan ini? *Seandainya dulu saya tahu* tidak punya tense, dan *akan* mencakup will dan would, jadi pelajar memasang *would* di kedua bagian atau memakai past simple. Periksa **bagian if**: situasi masa lalu → **had + bentuk ketiga**, dan tanpa *would*.
Kamu mungkin mendengar *If I would have known* dalam bahasa Inggris Amerika yang santai, tapi itu tidak baku: dalam tulisan, di kantor, dan saat tes, pakai **If I had known**.

blocks.text:
**could have / might have** can replace *would have* in the result:
- **could have** + third form = it was **possible**, there was a chance (*bisa*): *If she'd asked me, I **could have helped** her.*
- **might have** + third form = **maybe**, not sure (*mungkin*): *If we had left earlier, we **might have caught** the last MRT.*
- **would have** = you're sure about the result (*pasti*): *If I had known, I **would have come**.*

id.text:
**could have / might have** bisa menggantikan *would have* di bagian hasil:
- **could have** + bentuk ketiga = waktu itu **mungkin dilakukan**, ada kesempatan (*bisa*): *If she'd asked me, I **could have helped** her.*
- **might have** + bentuk ketiga = **mungkin**, tidak pasti: *If we had left earlier, we **might have caught** the last MRT.*
- **would have** = kamu yakin dengan hasilnya (*pasti*): *If I had known, I **would have come**.*

blocks.prompt: If Rina ___ the job advert, she would have applied for it.
blocks.explain: The result is *would have applied* (the past), so the if-part needs **had + third form**: *had seen*. *saw* makes it about now, and *would* never goes after *if*.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: If Rina ___ the job advert, she would have applied for it.
id.explain: Bagian hasilnya *would have applied* (masa lalu), jadi bagian if perlu **had + bentuk ketiga**: *had seen*. *saw* membuatnya jadi tentang sekarang, dan *would* tidak pernah dipakai setelah *if*.

id.title: Dua jebakan, serta could have / might have

blocks.text:
In speech, people shorten both **had** and **would** to **'d**: *If I'd known, I'd have come.* So how do you know which is which? Look at what comes **after** it:
- **'d + third form** (*known, gone, been, seen*) → **had**: *If I**'d known** = If I had known*
- **'d + have + third form** → **would**: *I**'d have come** = I would have come*
- **'d + base verb** (*go, be, like*) → **would**: *I**'d like**, I**'d be** happy*

And an easy check: in the **if-part**, **'d** is always **had**, because *would* never goes after *if*.

id.text:
Saat bicara, orang menyingkat **had** dan **would** menjadi **'d**: *If I'd known, I'd have come.* Jadi bagaimana cara membedakannya? Lihat kata **setelahnya**:
- **'d + bentuk ketiga** (*known, gone, been, seen*) → **had**: *If I**'d known** = If I had known*
- **'d + have + bentuk ketiga** → **would**: *I**'d have come** = I would have come*
- **'d + kata kerja dasar** (*go, be, like*) → **would**: *I**'d like**, I**'d be** happy*

Cara cek yang mudah: di **bagian if**, **'d** selalu **had**, karena *would* tidak pernah dipakai setelah *if*.

blocks.text: **would have** is often said very fast and weak: *would've*, which sounds like 'wud-ev', and *I'd have* sounds like 'aid-ev'. Because of the sound, even native speakers sometimes write *would of* ✗. Write **would have** or **would've** ✓. The same goes for **could've** and **might've**.

id.text: **would have** sering diucapkan sangat cepat dan lemah: *would've*, bunyinya seperti 'wud-ev', dan *I'd have* bunyinya seperti 'aid-ev'. Karena bunyinya, penutur asli pun kadang menulis *would of* ✗. Tulis **would have** atau **would've** ✓. Begitu juga **could've** dan **might've**.

blocks.prompt: Sari: 'If you'd booked earlier, we'd have got a cheaper ticket.' What do the two 'd mean?
blocks.explain: *you'd booked*: 'd + third form, in the if-part → **had**. *we'd have got*: 'd + have + third form → **would**.

id.prompt: Sari: 'If you'd booked earlier, we'd have got a cheaper ticket.' Apa arti kedua 'd itu?
id.explain: *you'd booked*: 'd + bentuk ketiga, di bagian if → **had**. *we'd have got*: 'd + have + bentuk ketiga → **would**.

material.title: Mixed: a different past, a different now

blocks.text:
Sometimes a past choice changes your life **now**. Then you mix: the if-part is the **imagined past** (third conditional), and the result is the **imagined present** (second conditional):
- **if + had + third form**, **would + base verb** (or **would be + -ing** for something happening now)

*If I had studied IT, I would have a different job now.* → I didn't study IT (past), and I don't have a different job (now).

**Look at the time words.** *now, today, still, at the moment* → **would + base verb**. *yesterday, last year, in 2019, then* → **would have + third form**.

id.text:
Kadang pilihan di masa lalu mengubah hidupmu **sekarang**. Kalau begitu, kamu mencampur: bagian if adalah **masa lalu khayalan** (third conditional), dan bagian hasil adalah **masa kini khayalan** (second conditional):
- **if + had + bentuk ketiga**, **would + kata kerja dasar** (atau **would be + -ing** untuk sesuatu yang sedang berlangsung sekarang)

*If I had studied IT, I would have a different job now.* → dulu saya tidak kuliah IT, dan sekarang pekerjaan saya tidak lain.

**Perhatikan kata waktunya.** *now, today, still, at the moment* → **would + kata kerja dasar**. *yesterday, last year, in 2019, then* → **would have + bentuk ketiga**.

rows.en: If I had studied IT, I would have a different job now.
rows.id: Seandainya dulu saya kuliah IT, sekarang pekerjaan saya pasti lain.

id.note: pilihan di masa lalu → akibat sekarang

rows.en: If Budi hadn't lost his passport, he would be in Tokyo today.
rows.id: Kalau saja Budi tidak kehilangan paspornya, hari ini dia sudah ada di Tokyo.

rows.en: If I had taken that job, I would be living in Jakarta now.
rows.id: Seandainya dulu saya ambil pekerjaan itu, sekarang saya tinggal di Jakarta.

rows.en: If I had taken that job, I would have moved to Jakarta in 2022.
rows.id: Seandainya dulu saya ambil pekerjaan itu, saya pasti sudah pindah ke Jakarta tahun 2022.

id.note: in 2022 → akibat di masa lalu → third conditional

blocks.text:
**Trap:** *I would be live in Jakarta now* ✗. After **would be**, use the **-ing** form: *I would **be living** in Jakarta now* ✓, or simply *I would **live** in Jakarta now* ✓. Indonesian *sekarang saya tinggal* has no -ing, so learners join *be* and the base verb.
And don't put a past result with *now*: *I wouldn't have been tired now* ✗ → *I **wouldn't be** tired now* ✓.
At B2 the meaning decides: the last two examples above are both correct, one about **now**, one about **then**.

id.text:
**Jebakan:** *I would be live in Jakarta now* ✗. Setelah **would be**, pakai bentuk **-ing**: *I would **be living** in Jakarta now* ✓, atau cukup *I would **live** in Jakarta now* ✓. *Sekarang saya tinggal* dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak punya -ing, jadi pelajar menggabungkan *be* dengan kata kerja dasar.
Dan jangan pasang akibat masa lalu dengan *now*: *I wouldn't have been tired now* ✗ → *I **wouldn't be** tired now* ✓.
Di level B2, artinya yang menentukan: dua contoh terakhir di atas sama-sama benar, satu tentang **sekarang**, satu tentang **waktu itu**.

blocks.text: **Note: the other way round.** Less often, the if-part is about **now or always**, and the result is in the **past**: *If I **spoke** Japanese, I **would have applied** for the Tokyo job last year.* → I don't speak Japanese (in general), so I didn't apply (last year). *If I **were** more organised, I **wouldn't have missed** the deadline yesterday.* You don't need to make these yet, but now you'll recognise them.

id.text: **Catatan: kebalikannya.** Lebih jarang, bagian if tentang **sekarang atau selalu**, dan hasilnya di **masa lalu**: *If I **spoke** Japanese, I **would have applied** for the Tokyo job last year.* → saya tidak bisa bahasa Jepang (secara umum), jadi tahun lalu saya tidak melamar. *If I **were** more organised, I **wouldn't have missed** the deadline yesterday.* Kamu belum perlu membuat kalimat seperti ini, tapi sekarang kamu bisa mengenalinya.

blocks.prompt: Rina bought a flat in Bandung in 2015. Today it's worth twice as much. Which sentence is about now?
options: If Rina hadn't bought the flat, she would have rented one in 2015.
If Rina hadn't bought the flat, she wouldn't be so rich now.
If Rina didn't buy the flat, she won't be rich now.
blocks.explain: **had + third form** (an imagined past) + **would + base verb** + *now* = a mixed conditional about the present. The first sentence is about 2015 (a past result). The third mixes the past simple and *won't*.

id.prompt: Rina membeli apartemen di Bandung tahun 2015. Sekarang harganya dua kali lipat. Kalimat mana yang tentang sekarang?
id.explain: **had + bentuk ketiga** (masa lalu khayalan) + **would + kata kerja dasar** + *now* = mixed conditional tentang sekarang. Kalimat pertama tentang 2015 (akibat di masa lalu). Kalimat ketiga mencampur past simple dan *won't*.

id.title: Mixed: masa lalu berbeda, masa kini berbeda

suggestedQuestions: Why is it 'If I had known' and not 'If I knew' when I talk about the past?
How can I tell if 'd means had or would?

id.intro: Selamat datang lagi! Kamu sudah bisa berandai-andai tentang masa kini dengan second conditional: If I had more time, I would learn Japanese. Hari ini kamu mundur ke masa lalu dan membayangkan masa lalu yang berbeda: If I had known about the meeting, I would have come (tapi waktu itu saya tidak tahu, dan saya tidak datang). Lalu kamu akan menghubungkan masa lalu yang berbeda dengan masa kini yang berbeda: If I had studied IT, I would have a different job now.
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa 'If I had known', bukan 'If I knew', kalau membicarakan masa lalu?
Bagaimana cara tahu 'd itu artinya had atau would?
Apa bedanya would have, could have dan might have?
Kapan saya pakai 'I would have' dan kapan 'I would be' setelah 'If I had …'?

assessment.tmc-1: Bulan lalu Rina ketinggalan pesawat ke Bali karena KRL-nya mogok. Lengkapi dengan kata kerja dalam kurung (pakai bentuk negatif): If the KRL ___ (not / break) down, she ___ (not / miss) her flight.
assessment.tmc-2: Perbaiki kesalahannya: If I would have left home earlier, I would have caught the train.
assessment.tmc-3: Terjemahkan ke dalam bahasa Inggris. Pakai could: Kalau saja waktu itu saya tahu nomor HP Budi, saya bisa meneleponnya.
assessment.tmc-4: Budi gagal ujian SIM minggu lalu, jadi sekarang dia berdiri di bus yang penuh sesak. Lengkapi dengan would dan kata kerja dalam kurung: If he had passed the test, he ___ (drive) to work right now.
assessment.tmc-5: Perbaiki kesalahannya: If I hadn't stayed up so late last night, I wouldn't have been tired now.
assessment.tmc-6: Sari sama sekali tidak tidur tadi malam, dan sekarang dia tidak bisa konsentrasi di kantor. Lengkapi ucapannya dengan kata kerja dalam kurung: 'If I ___ (sleep) better last night, I wouldn't feel so tired today.'
